meta.title: The Pintland Isles — Dynamics Simulator
meta.changes: your influence ranking: link strengths follow each item's tier and rank, Past / Now / Future sets each item's drift, the Bond Crisis and Cumstead Collapse are global, and the Warden heresy is gone
sources: THE PINTLAND ISLES — MASTER LORE COMPENDIUM
A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Concept Economy)

groups.name: The Parliament of the Liquor Kings
groups.description: Seamus Bonehardy, Jack Anqoak, Jagerbauhm, Guinnie, Buke and Jameson Pilsner — the Parliament of the Liquor Kings. Heroes of the Cloister Beast, the MAA and Maximilian; also blamed for Thatcher's death, a massacre, an assassination and a mountain of Stewards-era debt. Legitimacy genuinely contested.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (The Liquor Kings); Concepts I–VI

groups.name: Aleforge Mayoral Government
groups.description: The Bonehardy Administration. Seamus won the mayoral election after Drake's banishment and "has since done absolutely nothing in his tenure" — a fact called out by the other Kings — yet the town is calm and mostly supportive. Inherited the crisis-era bond debt; still employs John Rump as treasurer.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Aleforge — Modern History); Hall of Records (Mayoral Election Speeches)

groups.name: Church of Patmos (Providence)
groups.description: One office, three powers: Cardinal Addy's spire is Providence's government, its market regulator (it decrees what may be crafted or sold) and its church. Tithes flow upward at half of all earnings. Scholars whisper that ClockHeart Tonic binds souls to the church's will.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence); VI (The Church of Patmos)

groups.name: Roto Kaiishi Merchant-Philosophers
groups.description: The floating city Xi Jin Ping founded as a fence for pirate plunder. No sales tax, a flat yearly merchant fee, taboos instead of laws, and a hand-picked chain of merchant-philosopher heirs (Kim Jong Un) meant to stop the biggest players writing the rules.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Shanty Town & the Windsunk Council
groups.description: Lawless cliff settlement beside Sackbeard's Tavern. The Windsunk Council "decide who eats, who raids, and who gets tossed off the cliffs." Tide Callers, Coral-eyed, the Ashen Oath, and every crew its own little nation. Skeptical of any centralized power — the Kings included.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town; Political Factions; Foreign Relations)

groups.name: MAMA (Prohibitionist Insurgency)
groups.description: Heirs of the MAA (massacred by the Kings in a cave). Rose again as Mothers Against Maximilian's Assassination; secretly founded by Susan Plinket ("JR"). Plinket is sentenced to be Rollo's girlfriend and the cells are "rendered inoperable" — but the ideology that alcohol is moral corruption was never killed.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (The MAA / MAMA; Susan Plinket); Concept V

groups.name: Gideon Drake (Exiled)
groups.description: The Bastard Veil. Part-Veilwalker, Sackbeard's first mate and killer, former mayor who actually governed (Barley Road, subsidies, bonds, militia) — and John Cum's murderer, who framed MAMA for it. Banished to unexplored Vodkonia: long-lived, resourceful, desperate.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Gideon Drake); Concept V; XI (Open Mysteries)

groups.name: Aleforge Brewing & Export
groups.description: The Gilded Tankard's magic spring, Brewers Lane and Trials tourism — Aleforge is a single-export state and knows it. The Tankard's entire stockpile currently sits under Goldcoral control, sold in secret at Jack's Grog Galley.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Gilded Tankard); II (Aleforge)

groups.name: Goldcoral Incorporated
groups.description: "Aggressive mercantilism." Headquartered in Providence, but every real book is kept in Roto, where nobody asks. Privately owned by Jack Anqoak; seized the Gilded Tankard's stockpile after Wepple gambled the investment away.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (Goldcoral Incorporated)

groups.name: The Ducket (M2 Stability)
groups.description: The global inter-town trade currency; every town runs its own sub-economy and converts at exchange rates that move with story events. Total supply (M2) is meant to stay flat — almost nothing may create new Duckets, and the one feasible exception is an influx from an outside economy. Higher = a flatter, more trusted M2 and stabler conversion rates.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Global Currency; The Concept Economy)

groups.name: Ducket Velocity
groups.description: How fast Duckets change hands — the second number the Analysis tracks. "If M2 is flat and velocity is consistent after six months we're on the right track." Low velocity is coin buried in chests and a stalled economy; very high velocity on a flat M2 is inflation's other door.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Global Currency; To Those Drunk in the Back of the Room)

groups.name: Player Economy (Shops, Wages & Contracts)
groups.description: What the people of the Isles actually feel: shop stock and prices, restock rates, NPC wages, rotating town contracts. Driven top-down by the Concept Economy — players have little to no power over it. "As items get scarcer and more expensive, they feel that their town is struggling even if they don't know it's due to embargos." Shops restock with town prosperity, never below a floor.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Player Economy vs. Concept Economy)

groups.name: Banks & Credit
groups.description: The key intermediary between the player and concept economies: loans for land, ships and shops; holdings accounts paying small interest. The catch — that interest must come from loan income, never from minted coin. The credit market is young.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Banks and Insurance)

groups.name: Voyage Insurers
groups.description: Insurance began as a few people gambling on whether or not ships would return from voyages. "As unsexy as insurance is, gambling is smoking hot." Every Stormtide is claims season; every pirate raid is a payout.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Banks and Insurance)

groups.name: Roto Currency Black Market
groups.description: Where the posted exchange rates stop meaning anything. "A strong black market for currencies would be fun, obviously based in Roto" — and it fits Roto's taboo system exactly: not illegal, just sold after dark. Insider trading and arbitrage are features, not bugs.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Player Economy; Taxes and Treasuries); Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Aleforge Bond Market
groups.description: Instituted by Drake at low rates, expanded by the Kings during the Stewards crisis "at increasingly unfavorable interest rates." Roto traders are the big holders. Stat = market confidence; low values mean the debt is winning.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Aleforge Bond Market)

groups.name: The Cumstead Wheat Supply
groups.description: Aleforge's key grain source. Its plenty was the Veilwalker blessing on John Cum; Cum is dead (by Drake's hand), the fields saw blight and green Factory sludge, and John Rump — addict, embezzler — now holds it without the blessing.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (John Cum's Cumstead); Concept V

groups.name: Southern Bellows Nation (via StormVeil)
groups.description: The fog-wrapped, agnostic-by-law brewers of the worst IPAs in existence, only now cracking their isolation through illegal Ale Bean routes and a partnership with StormVeil Trading Co. Flagged by both the Aleforge Special Drinkers Unit and the Providence Guard. Nobody knows why they are reaching out.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (The Southern Bellows Nation); VI (Stormveil Trading Co.)

groups.name: The Drunken Trials
groups.description: The Isles' most important cultural event: magic ale from the Tankard's spring that never hangs you over but does strange things at volume. Crowns the Liquor Kings. Tourism engine, prestige engine, and — since the MAA raided the first one — a standing target.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Drunken Trials); Concept I

groups.name: Owe Block Underground
groups.description: The district Providence's disparity built. Crimson Cutters, Seaside Circus, Wagwan's Stank Tank, underground markets, and quiet Veilwalker sympathizers (Sexton Gobbler's shrine). The obligatory tithe was cut to 25% after Gobbler's disgrace.
groups.loreSource: Compendium IV (Founding of Owe Block); Concept IV

groups.name: Fenwick & the Veil Elders
groups.description: The cobbled hamlet on the marshy Fen, and the Elders who speak for it. Fenwick plays no politics until the flesh-born take too much; then "you can't predict what don't want anything" becomes a warning. Its economy is vows, not coin: flowers planted, lives lived virtuously, fishing lures and remedies in return.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers; Providence Foreign Relations); VI (Veilwalker Trade & Custom)

groups.name: Unknownism (Baba Paku's Mission)
groups.description: The missionary strand of the unknown-gods faith that walked out of Owe Block with Baba Paku, "explaining to anyone who will listen the secrets of Providence's main religion." Wants its first Owe Block Saint. Funds itself with arms dealing.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Baba Paku)

groups.name: Fayte Druids (Cloister Takeover)
groups.description: OPEN THREAD. A small movement, not a church: a handful of monks who commandeered the Cloister months ago — the Kings' own meeting hall, built over a hole to hell and a beast's prison dimension. Strange chants and lights. Purpose unknown; every link to them is speculative by design.
groups.loreSource: Compendium XI (Open Mysteries); II (The Cloister)

groups.name: The Veilwalkers (Earth-born)
groups.description: The earth-born. Nature spirits made them from soil to resist the flesh-born; neither nature nor man should conquer the other. They live tenfold a human span, trade in vows, not coin, curse the greedy with famine and disease, and transform into ghostly figures when they commune with the woodland spirits.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers); VI (Veilwalker Trade & Custom)

groups.name: The Flesh-born (Humans)
groups.description: Humanity as a lineage bloc: the barbarians whose conquest the earth-born were made to resist, and every town since. The baseline against which every other lineage's standing is measured.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers)

groups.name: Halfbreeds — the Line of Johns
groups.description: The only known human-Veilwalker line: John Cum (dead), John Rump (treasurer, holds the Cumstead), and plausibly Gideon Drake as distant ancestor. The Lagendale treaty template — fields blessed "so long as Walker blood remained in that family line" — is running again, live.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (John Cum; John Rump); IV (The Rotted Soul — The First Treaty)

groups.name: Aleforge Tax Take
groups.description: Tolls, docking fees, property and luxury tax — the Analysis's preferred revenue (income tax is unenforceable when anyone can bury coin in a chest in the woods). Taxes force money out of circulation, steer behaviour, and fund the treasury. Drake zeroed sea tolls and raised road tolls 50%. 50 = today's mix.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Taxes and Treasuries); Compendium III (Drake's policies)

groups.name: Aleforge Tariffs & Embargoes
groups.description: Mercantilism's first lever: aim for a positive balance of trade. Drake's cheap-grog import restriction, the 20% / 150% Veilwalker artifact tariff, and the tariff war with Providence where "each side [seeks] to choke the other's wealth." 50 = today.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy); Compendium II (Providence Foreign Relations)

groups.name: Patmos Tithe Rate
groups.description: The spire's cut. 50 = today: half of all earnings in Providence, a quarter in Owe Block since Gobbler's disgrace. The purest example of a treasury pulling coin out of pockets.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Church of Patmos); Concept IV

groups.name: Monopoly Charters
groups.description: Exclusive trade grants — a mercantilist government's favourite gift to its friends. Goldcoral is the obvious beneficiary; Roto was founded on the opposite principle.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy)

groups.name: Subsidized Industries
groups.description: Paying industries to outcompete rivals: Drake's wheat & barley subsidies and Gilded Tankard Grant, the Stewards-era guilds, Bonehardy's promised grain money, Buke's A.L.E. Financed, mostly, on Aleforge bond paper.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy); Concept V

groups.name: Concept Performance Rewards
groups.description: Stock options or currency granted by the gamemaster to top performers after each concept — paid from the town treasury, never minted. "Consistent top performers will gain immense wealth, however this may come at political costs."
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy)

groups.name: Seamus Bonehardy, "King of Kegs"
groups.description: Navigator, mutineers' son, and the sitting Mayor of Aleforge. Crafted the best trade deals of the Stewards era, was blackmailed by his own treasurer into legalizing the tonic, and has since been seen more in taverns than in town hall. One of only two Kings to leave the Rotted Soul's prison with his soul intact. Some read his "Ode to the Six" as a farewell to politics.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Seamus Bonehardy); Concept V (Individual Performance Summary)

groups.name: Jack Anqoak, "Oracle of Aleforge"
groups.description: Thief of Gyntonick, founder of Goldcoral Incorporated, owner of the Grog Galley and The Bastard's Requiem. Beat Wepple and seized the Tankard's stockpile. Spent weeks in Hoegaarden's stacks and led the Kings to the Rotted Soul, where he lost his soul. "A robber baron?"
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Jack Anqoak); VI (Goldcoral; Grog Galley); Hall of Records (Mayoral Election Speeches)

groups.name: Jagerbauhm, "Drunken Angel"
groups.description: Born in Shanty Town, raised a refugee in Providence, turned functional alcoholic by Faegi's bootleg ClockHeart Tonic at sixteen. Pro-Providence; exposed Susan Plinket; flew into the Dread Harrow with the artifacts and closed the portal. "Consistently sacrificed personal political reputation for Aleforge's wellbeing."
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Jagerbauhm); Concept V (The Resolution; Individual Performance Summary)

groups.name: Steph "Guinnie" O'Guinness
groups.description: Deserter who turned steel on his captain rather than torch a village near Fenwick, then won the Drunken Trials "quiet as a tide." Pro-Shanty Town and strongly pragmatic, yet the only King to vote for Veilwalker manifest destiny. Helped slam the Nethergate shut. "Blue flag 'til I'm buried."
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Guinnie); Concept V; Hall of Records (Guinnie's Reports; Mayoral Election Speeches)

groups.name: Buke (No Middle, No Last Name)
groups.description: Found as an infant in an empty whiskey barrel; the best fisherman in his village; chugged 17 pints in 180 seconds for a ticket to the Trials. Killed Maximilian, which not everyone calls just, and MAMA was born of it. Pro-ale production above all else, solved the portal problem, and was named a candidate for mayor.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Buke); Concept III; Concept V (Individual Performance Summary)

groups.name: Jameson Pilsner (JP)
groups.description: Born in a barren field soaked in whiskey and beer on the Coors Golden Isles, where drinking was religion and the IPA a fraud. Loves alcohol "too much to abuse it." Found Cumsock the goat, died three times in the final battle and was raised each time by Aleforge ale. Pro-Fenwick.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Jameson Pilsner); Concept V (Individual Performance Summary)

groups.name: Old Aleforge Municipal
groups.description: The last three offices of old Aleforge: the Comptroller (Hornithan Buttlube), the Sheriff (Edward Cocaine) and the Color Guard (Cpt. Lincoln Dillydally). Honorary by law and hereditary by blood, and they do not see it that way. They still try to hold onto power.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Aleforge: Old Aleforge Municipal)

groups.name: The ASDU & the Aleforge Militia
groups.description: The Aleforge Special Drinkers Unit and the volunteer militia Drake raised after the Trials riots. Captain Crawdad organized it against the hordes of interdimensional creatures. It flags the SBN, investigates missing persons at Hoegaarden, and has been trying to reach Rachel Zlurs for weeks.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Gideon Drake: Aleforge Militia; Captain Crawdad; Rachel Zlurs); II (SBN)

groups.name: The Providence Guard & the Friars
groups.description: Sergeant Hark's Guard, Hunk the Monk at the Cardinal's towers, and the Friars who roam the markets on Beastwatch "judging with a keen eye and a stricter hand." It watches Vlad the Kisser, flags the SBN, and once hunted the Kings for Sexton Gobbler.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence); III (Sergeant Hark; Hunk the Monk; Vlad the Kisser)

groups.name: Shanty Captains & Crews
groups.description: The lifeblood of Shanty Town: retired, rogue or rising captains who crashed here willingly or came to reclaim their legend. Each crew is its own little nation, and they don't always get along.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Political Factions)

groups.name: The Crimson Cutters
groups.description: Owe Block's mafia gang, Pope's old outfit from the Buenacera on Vanity Street. Jack, Seamus and Jagerbauhm ran with them during A Walk on Owe Block and were obliterated by the Seaside Circus.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Pope); IV (A Walk on Owe Block)

groups.name: The Seaside Circus
groups.description: The Cutters' rival gang, and the side that won the Owe Block gang war. Guinnie, as a street reaper, mowed down Crimson Cutters in every confrontation.
groups.loreSource: Compendium IV (A Walk on Owe Block)

groups.name: The Chronicles (Isles Press)
groups.description: The Aleforge Chronicle (eleven stories on Mr. BBL's posterior, one on the economy), the Owe Block Chronicle, and Sister Bertha, the "most honest woman" in Providence. The press decides what gets found out.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Sister Bertha); narration canon

groups.name: Hoegaarden Library & Embassy
groups.description: The oldest institution in the Isles, above the catacombs of Lagendale and the River Coffin. Holds the largest collection of books in the known waters, the records of the VeilRunner, classified manuscripts tied to Drake, and an embassy that sheltered the Kings from Gobbler's purchased law.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Hoegaarden Library); IV (Horror in Hoegaarden); Hall of Records

groups.name: Faith of the Brewmasters Deity
groups.description: Aleforge's own faith: the founders saved a brewmaster deity, who blessed the town with a spring of the finest ale. The deity enjoys revelry, cheer and the occasional chaos. Brewmasters Eve (each pint saves one soul from the Realm of the Soulless), Brewmasters Day, the founders' dance. Its dark mirror is Cedric the Vicar, beheaded for claiming to be the Deity reborn.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Aleforge: Founding; Cedric the Vicar; Trodon Hallis); VI (Holidays)

groups.name: Circs & Kalifarts (the Tonic Clergy)
groups.description: The Circs toil in hidden vats brewing ClockHeart Tonic with chants to the unknown gods; the Kalifarts, rare as a sober night, scribble variations in lofty towers, some say chasing a potion to raise the dead. The tonic is Providence's economy and its religion at once.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence: The Ways of Providence)

groups.name: The Whiskey Runners
groups.description: A missionary group that smuggled illegal tonic from Providence to Aleforge during the previous Cardinal's reign; they brought Hunk the Monk to Providence as a baby. Faith and contraband in the same satchel. Rump's legalized bootleg tonic gave them a market.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Hunk the Monk); Concept V (Rump's blackmail)

groups.name: Owe Block Veil Sympathizers
groups.description: Sexton Gobbler's hidden shrine, the Veil Oath book and Chalice, and Friar Leo's obsidian-and-amethyst chamber behind the stone button in the Church of the Monk. Patmos exposed one apostate; it did not expose the queue.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Sexton Gobbler; Friar Leo); IV (A Walk on Owe Block)

groups.name: The Tide Callers
groups.description: Shanty Town's semi-religious order of mystics, navigators and storm-readers: former helmsmen, weather witches and deep-sea interpreters who believe the ocean is a divine force that rewards devotion and punishes arrogance.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Political Factions)

groups.name: The Ashen Oath
groups.description: Hidden fanatics who believe the sea, pirates and grog have tainted the world. They keep the Night of the False Sun, abduct one "tainted" soul each Veilfrost, and want to purge the Shoals and burn the beast bones. "Most dangerous when ignored."
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Political Factions); VI (Holidays: Night of the False Sun)

groups.name: The Coral-eyed
groups.description: Once sailors and scavengers who spent far too long beneath the sea, trapped in wrecks, cursed by unknown gods, or "kissed by the trench." Now something less than human and more than drowned, and one of Shanty Town's factions.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Political Factions)

groups.name: Bully Hill Mines (Dig Dug)
groups.description: Dig Dug, Foreman of the Mines at the Basin at Bully Hill: one of the biggest employers in Owe Block and the source of most of the gold in Providence's treasury.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Dig Dug)

groups.name: StormVeil Trading Co.
groups.description: A fast-growing carrier built on the Albatross, a sky ship that imitates the lost Cloudrunners and runs on Wolendi wind stores. Its semi-legal trade with the Southern Bellows is the first crack in their isolation.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (Stormveil Trading Co.); II (SBN)

groups.name: Wolendi Wind Farms
groups.description: The Derecho family's East Wind farm off Aleforge and West Wind farm high in the Breakback Mountains: the near-universal source of the wind stores every Albatross needs.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Wolendi); III (Gale & Guster Derecho); VI (Stormveil)

groups.name: Wepple & the Gilded Tankard
groups.description: Glub Tuppus Wepple, the Tankard's gruff, kindly brewmaster: gambled away Goldcoral's investment, was beaten by Jack and lost his whole stock to him, now tends bar at the Grog Galley to watch it sold, and is developing a new brew in secret.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Wepple); VI (Grog Galley)

groups.name: Militia & ASDU Funding
groups.description: Drake's volunteer militia and the ASDU, funded from the castle. More money means more raids broken up and more caves cleared, and more coin out of the treasury.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Gideon Drake: Aleforge Militia)

groups.name: Drunken Trials Revival Fund
groups.description: Drake's fund to make each Trials "the best yet": skilled workers building the games. Tourism, prestige, and a standing provocation to every prohibitionist.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Gideon Drake: Drunken Trials Revival Fund)

groups.name: Crafting Edicts
groups.description: The church "decrees what may be crafted or sold." Tighter edicts mean more tithe-able order in the market and more trade pushed into Owe Block's underground.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence: Our economy stands firm but stern)

groups.name: Friar Market Patrols
groups.description: Friars roaming the cobbled streets on Beastwatch, judging the markets. The spire's order in daylight, resented in the lower terraces.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence)

groups.name: ClockHeart Tonic Rations
groups.description: How freely the spire hands out the tonic that keeps the Apostles awake, and, scholars whisper, binds their souls. Generous rations deepen devotion and cost the treasury; thin ones feed the Whiskey Runners.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence); VI (The Church of Patmos)

groups.name: The Council's Plunder Share
groups.description: The cut the Windsunk Council takes when it decides "who eats, who raids." A bigger share fills the Council's chests and empties the captains' patience.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town)

groups.name: Windsunk Council Rule
groups.description: How hard the Council rules: who gets tossed off the cliffs. Strong rule keeps the Ashen Oath in the shadows; it also chafes a town built on the first pour of freedom.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town; Political Factions)

groups.name: Open Docks for Drifters
groups.description: Drifters, traders and travellers: merchants, exiles, scholars and outcasts moving between Shanty Town, Roto and beyond. "Some are spies. Some are saints. Some are completely mad."
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Political Factions)

groups.name: Roto's Flat Merchant Fee
groups.description: No sales tax, just a flat yearly fee for every merchant. Raise it and the council is richer; raise it too far and trade moves to the lower stilts after dark.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Taboo Enforcement
groups.description: Roto has taboos instead of laws, and the dedicated security forces the elite asked for after Xi's death. Enforcing them is the only brake on the night market.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: The Heir's Schooling
groups.description: Xi's hand-picked chain of merchant-philosopher heirs, trained in his principles as "an important counterweight to the corrupting effects of market domination."
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Vows Asked in Trade
groups.description: What Fenwick asks for its lures, remedies and guidance: flowers planted, lives lived virtuously. Ask more and the Veil's bounty grows dearer; ask less and the islanders forget what they owe.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (Veilwalker Trade & Custom)

groups.name: The Elders Hear Grievances
groups.description: Whether the Elders listen when a Walker comes forsaken. The 33rd Council did not, and Lagendale fell.
groups.loreSource: Compendium IV (The Rotted Soul: the Wronged Walker)

groups.name: Walkers at the Treeline
groups.description: Walkers standing watch where the fields meet the Brandywine Brush. A guarded edge makes plunder of spirit-marked land expensive.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers)

groups.name: Aleforge ⇄ Providence
groups.description: A brittle truce, strained by trade and theology: the Monk was exiled from Aleforge, and the tariff war has each side seeking to choke the other's wealth.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence Foreign Relations)

groups.name: Aleforge ⇄ Shanty Town
groups.description: Shanty sells Aleforge its crews and mocks its brew-god; it is skeptical of any centralized power, the Kings included.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Foreign Relations: On Aleforge)

groups.name: Aleforge ⇄ Roto Kaiishi
groups.description: Drake's Roto free-trade deal, and Roto traders holding most of Aleforge's bond paper.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Drake's policies); VI (Aleforge Bond Market)

groups.name: Aleforge ⇄ Fenwick
groups.description: Wystan Miller's old trade with Fenwick, the Veilwalker artifact tariff, and one King's vote for manifest destiny.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Golden Taps); Hall of Records (Mayoral Speeches)

groups.name: Providence ⇄ Shanty Town
groups.description: "We trade little with them." Shanty calls Providence a gilded pisshole; Providence calls Shanty a raucous pit. Cardinal Addy's mother was from Shanty Town.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence; Shanty Town's Foreign Relations)

groups.name: Providence ⇄ Roto Kaiishi
groups.description: A fleet of stout ships carries brewing gear to Roto and returns with the red-earth mineral that glows in the tonic's fire.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence)

groups.name: Providence ⇄ Fenwick
groups.description: "Quiet harmony, unmarred by tariffs": tonic sent sparingly as goodwill, fishing gear and remedies in return.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence Foreign Relations: A Relationship of Mutual Respect)

groups.name: Shanty Town ⇄ Roto Kaiishi
groups.description: Roto began as the fence for Shanty's plunder; now it runs without rules and that spooks the Windsunk Council. "Fence-lickers and coin-worshippers."
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Foreign Relations: On Roto)

groups.name: Shanty Town ⇄ Fenwick
groups.description: "We ain't stupid enough to piss off the woods." Offerings at the treeline, lures from the Fen.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town's Foreign Relations: On Fenwick)

groups.name: Roto Kaiishi ⇄ Fenwick
groups.description: Little direct contact: Roto trades in coin, Fenwick in vows.
groups.loreSource: extrapolated

groups.name: Stance toward Providence
groups.description: How warmly Aleforge treats Providence: trade terms, envoys, favours and slights. 50 = today's footing. The other town notices, and answers in kind.
groups.loreSource: Town relations

groups.name: Stance toward Shanty Town

relationships.short: the Kings now wear the mayor's chain
relationships.explanation: Bonehardy is a sitting Liquor King and the elected mayor — the Kings are no longer external heroes, their standing is the administration's standing, for better or worse.
relationships.precedent: Seamus Bonehardy elected mayor after the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: Bonehardy's record is every King's record
relationships.explanation: The entanglement cuts both ways: the administration's do-nothing calm (or any future fiasco) is laid at the whole Parliament's door, as the other Kings found when they publicly called Seamus out.
relationships.precedent: Bonehardy "has since done absolutely nothing in his tenure"

relationships.short: the Kings crush what they can see
relationships.explanation: When the Kings are strong they do what they have always done to prohibitionists: find the camp and clear it.
relationships.precedent: The cave massacre of the MAA; the raid on the MAMA camp beneath the abandoned shrine

relationships.explanation: Past a point, Kingly power stops deterring and starts recruiting. Every massacre left a mourner behind a rock — the MAA's left Maximilian, Maximilian's left MAMA. This is the Wronged Walker template: a grievance nobody bothers to resolve, returning later and larger.
relationships.precedent: MAA massacre → Maximilian; Maximilian's assassination → MAMA

relationships.explanation: MAMA's method is organized revolt timed for low morale, then blaming the Kings — Plinket's standing plan was to rise "if morale drops below 30% in any sector."
relationships.precedent: Plinket's revolt during the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: the Trials become a target again
relationships.explanation: Prohibitionists have always gone for the festival first; a stronger MAMA means guarded kegs, thinner crowds and nervous tourists.
relationships.precedent: The MAA raid on Aleforge during the first Drunken Trials

relationships.explanation: After their raid failed, the MAA waged guerrilla warfare "against the unsober people of Aleforge" — brewing is the economy they want dead.
relationships.precedent: MAA guerrilla campaign after the Drunken Trials

relationships.explanation: Plinket signed as "JR" precisely to shift suspicion onto the treasurer. Any MAMA resurgence drags John Rump's name back through the mud whether or not he did anything (he usually did something).

relationships.short: militia and amnesty hold the line
relationships.explanation: A confident administration can do both halves of what kept MAMA down: Drake's volunteer militia and the Kings' amnesty deal.
relationships.precedent: Gideon's Aleforge Militia; the MAMA amnesty deal (Jagerbauhm the lone vote against)

relationships.explanation: Pirate freedom is an oppositional identity. The more the Kings look like an empire, the louder the Windsunk Council's "we end wars" posture and the more Aleforge youth sneak off to be pirates.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty on Aleforge: "fun at parties, dangerous with power"

relationships.short: a strong crown keeps an exile exiled
relationships.explanation: Drake was banished by the Kings' tribunal; his road back runs through their weakness, exactly as his first rise did while they were off celebrating the Cloister Beast.
relationships.precedent: Drake's election while the Kings "were nowhere to be seen"

relationships.short: the Kings are the Trials' headliners
relationships.explanation: The Trials crown Liquor Kings; famous Kings make the Trials famous. Their legend is the festival's marketing.
relationships.precedent: The six-way tie that began the Age of the Six Kings

relationships.short: Jack's purse is a King's purse
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral is privately owned by a sitting King; the Parliament's fortunes and Goldcoral's ships travel together (Cheeks fled to Providence on one).
relationships.precedent: Jack founds Goldcoral after the Last Pour; Cheeks' escape on a Goldcoral ship

relationships.explanation: Drake genuinely governed — the Barley Road, subsidies, the militia — and Aleforge once chose his "order and stability over the Liquor Kings' chaotic legacy." News of him moving takes a season or two to curdle into nostalgia at the castle.
relationships.precedent: Drake's mayoralty and the Stewards scandal

relationships.short: the exile makes the Kings look careless
relationships.explanation: Every rumour of Drake's scheming reads as the Kings' failure: they let him rise, then let him walk away alive.
relationships.precedent: Drake banished rather than executed after the Dread Harrow

relationships.explanation: "Extremism alienates moderate and decent discourse." Drake put down an MAA-inspired riot personally in his first days — then used a fake MAMA note to cover his own murder.
relationships.precedent: Drake on the front line of the inauguration riot; the staged MAMA note at Cum's body

relationships.explanation: Drake killed John Cum and is plausibly the Line of Johns' distant ancestor. A stronger Drake is an existential threat to Rump — or a claimant to whatever the blood is worth.
relationships.precedent: Cum's murder; the Corrupted Ancestry compass

relationships.explanation: The scandal that toppled Drake was letters to Roto's leadership about illegal trade in Factory artifacts. Drake with money means Roto's grey market with more stock.
relationships.precedent: The courier's letters that opened the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: a steady Aleforge leaves no vacuum
relationships.explanation: Drake's pitch has always been "the Kings aren't here." A functioning mayoralty takes the pitch away.
relationships.precedent: Drake's original rise amid Thatcher's death and the Kings' absence

relationships.short: the Cardinal's voice is the law
relationships.explanation: In Providence religious authority *is* government: "his will the law of the land." Devotion converts straight into political control with no parliament in between.
relationships.precedent: Cardinal Addy commands from Patmos's spire

relationships.short: the church decrees what may be sold
relationships.explanation: The spire controls what may legally be crafted or sold; more control means more of the economy routed through Friars' market judgments and Sexton tithe-carts.
relationships.precedent: Friars judging the markets on Beastwatch

relationships.short: tithe gold funds the cryptic agenda
relationships.explanation: Half of all earnings flow into the church's coffers, "fueling a cryptic agenda" — tonic research, Kalifart towers, the red-earth bell. Money becomes ritual a season later.
relationships.precedent: The 50% tithe; the Kalifarts' search for a tonic to raise the dead

relationships.explanation: Whispered, unconfirmed: ClockHeart Tonic binds souls to Patmos's will. Past a threshold of devotion, social order stops being chosen and starts being dosed — the night-time revelry is the mask slipping.
relationships.precedent: Scholars' rumours that the tonic binds souls; Providence's dual day/night nature

relationships.explanation: Owe Block was founded out of Providence's religious and economic disparity. Tighten the tithe and the underclass district's informal economy expands to compensate; loosen it and money comes back above ground.
relationships.precedent: Founding of Owe Block; the tithe cut to 25% after Gobbler's disgrace

relationships.explanation: Extraction takes a season to become recruitment — the Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus fill their ranks from the tithe-broke.
relationships.precedent: A Walk on Owe Block: the gang wars

relationships.short: Friars clamp down on the district
relationships.explanation: Where the spire can enforce, underground culture goes quiet; when its grip slips, the Stank Tank gets loud.
relationships.precedent: Gobbler's purchased law enforcement hunting the Kings

relationships.short: order and the underground are zero-sum
relationships.explanation: Patmos social order and Owe Block culture are defined against each other — the district exists because the order has no room for it.

relationships.short: brewing tools out, red-earth mineral in
relationships.explanation: Roto is Providence's chief trade partner: brewing gear and rare tonic out, silks, spices and the red-earth mineral for the prayer bell in.
Goldcoral is headquartered in Providence and sells its profits to Providence's wealthy, who "only see what they want to see."
Aleforge tried a Patmos mayor once. Bronco Chestnut was "deeply unpopular and quickly voted out of office." Patmos zeal abroad reads as a threat at home.
After Gobbler's hidden Veilwalker shrine, Addy "turned the scandal into doctrine." Orthodox strength means hunted shrines and Veil sympathizers keeping their heads down.
relationships.precedent: Sexton Gobbler's apostasy; the Day of Hollow Tongues

relationships.explanation: Baba Paku preaches the church's "secrets" to anyone who will listen; a vigilant spire does not appreciate its secrets being street-preached by an arms dealer.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku; the Day of Hollow Tongues

relationships.explanation: Patmos publicly preaches "order, sobriety, devotion." The prohibitionist current borrows that moral vocabulary — hypocrisy about the tonic notwithstanding.
relationships.precedent: Patmos public doctrine; Bronco Chestnut's theocratic push in Aleforge

relationships.explanation: Providence views the Trials as pagan excess and hosts its own solemn rites; a culturally ascendant Patmos draws pilgrims and prestige away from the festival.
Rump's addiction runs on bootleg ClockHeart, still illegal in Providence where it is made. A tighter spire squeezes supply, and a squeezed addict with the treasury keys does something desperate.
relationships.precedent: Rump blackmails Bonehardy into legalizing bootleg tonic

relationships.explanation: A Patmos past its usual zeal hardens the Windsunk Council — Shanty remembers Providence as "a driftwood sermon by some tonic-made monk" and talks openly about cracking its lake port.
relationships.precedent: Jasper "no Eyes, all-Hands": "We call them next on the list."

relationships.explanation: Owe Block's gangs, bought police and hidden shrines are how Patmos control fails in practice.
relationships.precedent: Gobbler's corruption; the Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus

relationships.explanation: Unrest in Owe Block sends people to Aleforge looking for work outside Church control; they arrive as farmhands and mouths on a Cumstead already producing without its blessing.
relationships.precedent: Emergency Providence wheat deals during the blight; Guinnie's "blight blues"

relationships.explanation: Owe Block hides real Veilwalker sympathy — an obsidian-and-amethyst shrine behind a stone button in the Church of the Monk. When the district is culturally loud, the shrines get visitors.
relationships.precedent: The Veilwalker shrine found in A Walk on Owe Block

relationships.short: the district wants its first Saint
relationships.explanation: Unknownism is Owe Block's export; Baba Paku's ambition to be the first Owe Block Saint rides on the district's pride.
Baba Paku funds the mission with arms dealing. A booming mission is a booming gun trade.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku's "shady businesses such as arms dealing"

relationships.explanation: Every convert Baba Paku makes on a street corner is one who heard the church's secrets from an Owe Block arms dealer instead of from the spire.
"They don't regulate us, we don't raid them." A stronger Windsunk Council leans on that balance.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: "a delicate, grizzled detente"

relationships.short: Roto's elite want the reefs "cleaned up"
relationships.explanation: Roto's merchant-lords have floated cleaning up the pirate factions on the outer reefs; a centralized Roto is the Council's nightmare.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: Current Tensions

relationships.short: pirates skip the cliffs for Roto
relationships.explanation: Easy Roto profits pull Shanty-born pirates straight past the cliffs, thinning the Council's crews.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: pirates "chasing easier profits and softer landings"

relationships.explanation: Roto was built as the pirates' one reliable fence; a booming market pays better for what Shanty crews bring in.
The Windsunk Council has murmured about hitting an Aleforge keg shipment "just to remind 'em who the sea belongs to."
relationships.precedent: Old Salty on Aleforge: Current Tensions

relationships.explanation: Shanty's drinking culture is half the Trials' audience and a steady supply of competitors; Aleforge's young "sneak off to become pirates" and come back for the festival.
Aleforge is a single-export state — the risk Drake tried to diversify away from with the Thatcher Scholarship. Brewing receipts are the tax base.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Brewers Tax and Thatcher Memorial Scholarship

relationships.explanation: A flush treasury funds the brewers — the Gilded Tankard Grant, the Kings' guilds, local barrel manufacture.
relationships.precedent: Gilded Tankard Grant; Stewards-era guilds and barrel localization

relationships.explanation: The festival runs on Tankard output; a strong brewing sector pays for bigger games.
Trials tourism is Aleforge's second export; festival crowds pay tolls, docking fees and luxury tax.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Revival Fund goal: "attract tourism during the games"

relationships.explanation: Aleforge's kegs "showin' up in towns far west" is the Trials' fame converted into orders.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty: "their festival's drawn more visitors than a sea-witch's curse"

relationships.short: the Trials are the Kings' mandate
relationships.explanation: The Kings' only formal legitimacy is having won the Trials. A revered festival is a revered crown.
relationships.precedent: Thatcher Sr. reinstating the annual Trials; the six-way tie

relationships.short: every Trials is a recruiting poster
relationships.explanation: The prohibitionists were born opposing "the culture of drinking that the Drunken Trials perpetuated"; the bigger the party, the better the sermon against it.

relationships.short: real ale trade diverted to Roto books
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral routes real profit through Roto specifically to dodge scrutiny. As Jack's leverage grows, more of Aleforge's actual ale trade flows through Goldcoral's books rather than the town's brewers and treasury.
relationships.precedent: Jack seizes the Gilded Tankard's stockpile after Wepple's gambling losses

relationships.short: profits that never touch the treasury
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral "brings a lot of profits in but not much transparency" — the Wepple Ale sold at the Grog Galley pays no Aleforge brewers tax.
relationships.precedent: Wepple Ale sold in secret at Jack's Grog Galley

relationships.short: the original books live in Roto
relationships.explanation: All of Goldcoral's trade and its true ledgers run through Roto's low-regulation markets.

relationships.short: the robber baron buys a voice
relationships.explanation: Money becomes leverage: Bonehardy's campaign warned Jack would "leverage his position… to get better deals for his trade company."
relationships.precedent: Bonehardy's election remarks on Jack Anqoak

relationships.explanation: Jack ran for mayor on the Kings' "ungodly amounts of debt" and Rump's embezzlement; Goldcoral's political weight is opposition weight.

relationships.short: taking too much from the earth
relationships.explanation: Aggressive mercantilism strips herbs, game and spirit-marked stones; those who "take too much from the earth" are haunted by famine and disease. The Veil's standing erodes first, the curse follows.
relationships.precedent: Young pirates plundering Fenwick lands; the Veilwalker curse

relationships.explanation: Opaque profits and secret stockpile sales mean trade no town can see or price; conversion rates drift.
Bond confidence tracks whether the treasury can service Stewards-era debt.
The Kings issued later rounds "at increasingly unfavorable interest rates" precisely because the crisis looked unstable.
Roto traders were "especially happy to buy these bonds." An Aleforge debt scare is a hole in Roto's books.
relationships.precedent: Drake's bond issue; Roto's enthusiastic buying

relationships.explanation: When Roto is flush, it buys Aleforge debt; when it isn't, nobody else will.
Every town converts its sub-economy to Duckets for inter-town trade; a shaky Ducket makes Aleforge's export receipts worth less.
relationships.precedent: Economy Pitch: towns convert at story-driven rates

relationships.explanation: Roto is where Duckets change hands most; its margins live on stable rates.
Half of all Providence earnings convert into church coffers; a debased Ducket is a debased tithe.
Healthy Roto markets keep enough honest trade moving to hold the Ducket's value steady.
relationships.precedent: Roto as the Isles' trading hub

relationships.explanation: Roto traders once "flooded the market with cheap and disgusting grog"; Drake restricted grog imports to protect Aleforge's key export.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Roto Free Trade Deal and grog restrictions

relationships.explanation: Ale Beans and finished IPAs are coming north on illegal routes; disgusting or not, they compete for tankards — the Roto grog flood all over again.
relationships.precedent: SBN illegal trade routes; StormVeil partnership

relationships.explanation: The Ducket supply is meant to be flat. Smuggled trade with a nation outside every town's ledgers moves value nobody can see, and the rates drift a season later.
relationships.precedent: SBN smuggling; the Economy Pitch's flat-M2 rule

relationships.explanation: The Providence Guard has flagged the SBN — a state where "agnosticism is law" is doctrinal irritation for a theocracy.
relationships.precedent: SBN flagged by the Providence Guard

relationships.explanation: The Cumstead is Aleforge's key grain source; when it falters, brewing falls with it (and a good harvest helps less than a bad one hurts).
relationships.precedent: Cum's grieving year: "a poor year's harvest" and ale production down

relationships.explanation: The Lagendale treaty template: the Veil blesses fields "so long as a human with Walker blood remained in that family line." The Cumstead's yield tracks how honoured that blood is — with a season's lag, like any harvest.
relationships.precedent: The First Treaty; John Cum's blessing

relationships.explanation: The blessing is the Veil's to give. Earth-born in good standing still tend the land that pleases them; diminished, they withdraw.
relationships.precedent: John Cum "spent years learning from the Veilwalkers"

relationships.explanation: Every mayor since Drake has promised the farmers money — Drake's wheat subsidies, Bonehardy's grain subsidies, Buke's A.L.E.
relationships.precedent: Barley and Wheat Subsidies; election speeches

relationships.explanation: John Rump is still Aleforge's treasurer, still addicted, still embezzling. The more secure his position, the more the ledger bleeds.
relationships.precedent: Mr. BBL's findings: Rump's confirmed embezzlement

relationships.explanation: Wheat is the Isles' staple input; failed harvests mean emergency imports paid out in Duckets.
relationships.precedent: Emergency Providence wheat deals during the blight

relationships.explanation: When the blight struck, Aleforge bought wheat from Providence. The Cumstead's loss is the spire's sale.
relationships.precedent: Stewards of Aleforge: emergency Providence wheat deals

relationships.explanation: The Veil was made to resist flesh-born conquest; flesh-born ascendancy is, by definition, the earth-born losing ground. Guinnie's "Veilwalker manifest destiny" vote is this edge in miniature.
relationships.precedent: The birth of the Veilwalkers; Guinnie's manifest-destiny vote

relationships.short: the earth takes back its due
relationships.explanation: Offend the Veil and "they'd just let the earth take us back" — famine and disease on those who take too much.
The Wronged Walker was dismissed because his case "crossed racial lines" and "made everyone uncomfortable." A flesh-born order sure of itself has little room for the half-blood.
The treaty made the halfbreed line the Veil's concern; earth-born standing lends the Johns theirs.

relationships.short: custom is what keeps the Walkers whole
relationships.explanation: The Elders' law — the Vow of Mate, the refusal to spill Walker blood — is the Veil's cohesion. Strong custom, strong people.
relationships.precedent: The Vow of Mate; Veilwalker law

relationships.explanation: Veilwalker trade *is* religion: fishing gear for a promise to plant a flower. When the custom spreads, the faith deepens.
Gobbler was a Sexton. Veil devotion recruits from inside the spire's own ranks.

relationships.short: the accord: wind when all winds fail
relationships.explanation: Pirates who keep the unspoken accord get healed, guided, and "sometimes gift[ed] with wind." A respected Veil is a luckier fleet.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Fenwick: Political Balance

relationships.explanation: However the Druids' rites work, they are working from inside the Kings' seat. Devotion there is possession.

relationships.short: the Kings' hall is not theirs
relationships.explanation: The Kings use the Cloister as their meeting hall and leave decisions to its magic lights. Someone else holding it is a humiliation and a lost instrument of power.
relationships.precedent: The Cloister: the Kings' meeting hall

relationships.short: the Kings could take it back
relationships.explanation: A strong Parliament has the swords to reclaim the Cloister.
Shanty's nightmare about the Cloister is specific: if its power wakes, the cliffs next door pay first. Past a point, Druid fervour starts emptying Shanty's taverns.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty: "If they unleash somethin'? It's our cliffs that'll catch the tide first."

relationships.explanation: Each season below par, coupons on the Stewards-era bonds come due and the treasury pays them. "The downside: they also accumulated significant national debt that they left for their successors."

relationships.short: the harvest sets the brewing season
relationships.explanation: Every season, the Cumstead's real output — not the price, the grain — decides how much the brewers can mash.
The tithe isn't a one-off; each season of heavy extraction pushes more of Owe Block's life into the informal economy.
Leadership neutralized, base intact. Every season the belief persists above its floor, a few more people start meeting in caves.
Roto traders reprice Aleforge bonds every season against the treasury's real position.
Embezzlement is a habit, not an event. As long as Rump keeps the treasury keys, the leak runs.
Without the blessing's bearer the Cumstead drifts toward whatever the blood's standing can sustain.
relationships.precedent: The blessing is "no longer applied" under Rump

relationships.short: the Grog Galley keeps selling Wepple Ale
relationships.explanation: The seized stockpile is sold in secret season after season — Aleforge's best brew, earning for Goldcoral.
relationships.precedent: Wepple Ale at Jack's Grog Galley

relationships.explanation: Drake is long-lived and patient. Whatever he gathers in Vodkonia turns into plans.
relationships.precedent: Drake "plotting his next moves" in Vodkonia

relationships.explanation: The annual feast falls in Stormtide. A well-loved festival fills the Tankard and the docks for a season; a diminished one leaves unsold kegs.
The last Keg of the year, every pirate gathers at the Tavern in peace. A strong ethos turns the feast into a show of Council strength.
relationships.precedent: Hoppy Holidays; the annual pirate gathering

relationships.explanation: Shop income comes only from existing Duckets moving through player-to-shop and NPC-to-shop trade. When circulation slows, tills empty and restocks slip.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: velocity tracking; the closed-loop Player Economy

relationships.explanation: Town currency exchanges run at set rates that update with story events; a shaky Ducket reprices every shelf in the Isles.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: currency exchanges in each town

relationships.explanation: Taxes and wages flow into the treasury, which resets how much NPCs can spend each day and sizes the rotating town contracts. A rich Aleforge posts better work.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "Contracts… with fluctuating rewards based on the size of the town treasury"

relationships.short: Providence shops restock with the spire
relationships.explanation: Ambient town shops pay straight into the treasury and restock with town prosperity; Providence's cheap, high-quality armour and weapons depend on the spire staying rich.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: Providence's better access to armour and weapons

relationships.explanation: Roto is where scarce goods come from when a town's own manufacturing falls short.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: shop availability depends on trade relations

relationships.explanation: The one way players push back up the chain: their buying and selling is velocity. Otherwise, players "have little to no impact on the Concept Economy."
relationships.precedent: Analysis: Player Economy vs. Concept Economy

relationships.short: too-fast money is inflation's other door
relationships.explanation: M2 times velocity is what chases the goods. Past a point, money changing hands faster than goods are made bids prices up even with a flat supply.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "Duckets chase a limited supply of goods"

relationships.short: tolls and fees fill the treasury
relationships.explanation: Docking fees, road tolls, property and luxury tax are how money leaves player pockets and lands in the treasury — the loop that funds everything else.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: Taxes and Treasuries; Drake's road-toll increase

relationships.short: taxes pull coin out of circulation
relationships.explanation: The first reason the Analysis gives for taxes: forcing money out of the system to fight inflation. The price is slower circulation.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "it can help stop the inflation problem by forcing money out of the system"

relationships.explanation: Every new toll booth on the Barley Road is a grievance at the castle gate.
Thatcher taxed breweries by production; Drake cut to a lower flat rate "to increase profit and local private investment." Raise the take and the brewers feel it first.
Drake eliminated sea tolls precisely to draw trade from Roto and Providence. Put them back and the ships go elsewhere.
Drake restricted cheap grog imports "to protect Aleforge's key export until other industries have grown."
relationships.precedent: Drake's Roto Free Trade Deal (grog restrictions)

relationships.explanation: Roto's traders are the ones a high Aleforge tariff wall is built to keep out.
relationships.precedent: The Roto grog flood before Drake's mayoralty

relationships.explanation: Tariffs between Aleforge and Providence "rise like storm tides, each side seeking to choke the other's wealth."
The Analysis's own example: items get scarcer and pricier, and people feel their town struggling without knowing it's an embargo.

relationships.short: what can't clear customs clears after dark
relationships.explanation: Every tariff wall creates an arbitrage, and arbitrage lives in Roto's night market.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: insider trading and arbitrage "a feature of the economy"

relationships.explanation: Drake taxed every Veilwalker gift 20% (150% if smuggled). Tariffs on vow-trade make the custom costlier to practise.
The tithe is the spire's treasury; the rate is the lever the Cardinal actually pulls.
relationships.precedent: The 50% tithe; the Owe Block cut to 25%

relationships.short: coin climbs the spire and stops moving
relationships.explanation: Tithed Duckets flow into coffers funding a "cryptic agenda," not back into the market.
A monopoly charter is the cleanest mercantilist gift there is, and Goldcoral — owned by a sitting King — is first in line.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "monopoly charters" as a main economic lever

relationships.explanation: Xi believed that if the biggest players controlled the market they would write rules that "gut Roto from the bottom up." Charters elsewhere pull the big players out of Roto's open market.
Charters narrow who may sell; shoppers pay the difference.
Drake's wheat subsidies went mostly to John Cum; Bonehardy and Buke both ran on more. It takes a season for money to become seed and farmhands.
The Gilded Tankard Grant: the town paying directly to upgrade brewing and exports.
Every subsidy is a treasury outflow; Aleforge has historically covered them with bonds.
relationships.precedent: Stewards of Aleforge: debt left for successors

relationships.explanation: Performance rewards tie player achievement back into the economy — and the Kings are the players.

relationships.short: out of the treasury, not the mint
relationships.explanation: Rewards are paid from the town treasury "to avoid infinite money grants after concepts."

relationships.short: the political cost of immense wealth
relationships.explanation: "Consistent top performers will gain immense wealth, however this may come at political costs." Kings paid from the treasury is a gift to anyone arguing they rule for themselves.
Bonehardy called Jack a robber baron on the debate stage; paying all six from the treasury invites the label for the rest.
A young credit market holds what paper there is — and Aleforge bonds are most of it.

relationships.short: loans for land, ships and shops
relationships.explanation: Players will need loans to buy land, ships and shops; healthy banks open those doors a season later.
Lending puts idle holdings back into circulation.
"The tricky part here is paying out interest on holdings without creating new Duckets." An overextended bank paying interest it hasn't earned from loans is minting by another name.

relationships.short: a failed underwriter drags its lender
relationships.explanation: Voyage wagers are written on credit; when the ships don't return, the banks find out who was gambling with their money.
Merchants sail when someone will cover the hull.
Roto's gamblers and merchants are the natural underwriters of the Isles' shipping.

relationships.short: the posted rate stops meaning anything
relationships.explanation: A strong currency black market prices Duckets against everything at whatever the lantern-holder says; official rates lose their grip.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "a strong black market for currencies… based in Roto"

relationships.explanation: In Roto nothing is illegal, only taboo — the night market pays the same flat merchant fee.

relationships.short: real books need a real fence
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral's original books live in Roto; its opaque profits need changing somewhere nobody records.
Illegal SBN trade arrives in currencies no town exchange quotes.

relationships.short: a trusted Ducket starves the night market
relationships.explanation: When the posted rate is honest, nobody pays the lantern premium.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: currency exchanges at set rates

relationships.explanation: The Analysis's first worry: "large farms exchanging one type of item for infinite currency." A Cumstead booming past its needs becomes exactly that farm.
Shanty Town trades by barter; "a simple barter system will loop around" any Ducket tax, and a Shanty boom moves less coin than it moves grog.
Above today's level, every season of subsidy is another bond round at a worse rate.

relationships.short: the tax take, season after season
relationships.explanation: Taxes are a standing inflow: above today's level they refill the treasury each season; below it they don't.
Each season above today's rate pushes more of Owe Block's life off the books.
Dangerous seas and Shanty raiders make Stormtide the season underwriters pay out. Pivot sits low: even a quiet Shanty sinks ships in Stormtide.
relationships.precedent: Pintland Calendar: Stormtide; Shanty Town's raiding threats

relationships.explanation: Calm seas and full sails: Goldsun is when coin moves.

relationships.short: Brewers Lane pride feeds the festival
relationships.explanation: The Trials are Aleforge's brewing culture on show. When the young brewers of Brewers Lane are proud of their craft, the festival has something to celebrate.
relationships.precedent: Beckoning the New Brews (Aleforge coming-of-age holiday)

relationships.explanation: Every Trials sends a few more youths into the brewhouses hoping to be named in the Gilded Tankard's walls.
relationships.precedent: Winners' names etched in the Gilded Tankard

relationships.explanation: A town that honours its brewers gets better beer a season later, and better beer exports.
The prohibitionist current frames alcohol itself as corruption; where it spreads, brewing stops being an honour.

relationships.short: Xi's principles keep the heirs honest
relationships.explanation: Roto's government is a chain of hand-picked heirs trained in Xi's principles. The culture of those principles is what keeps the chain from breaking.
relationships.precedent: Xi's succession system; Kim Jong Un

relationships.short: taboos keep dark trade after dark
relationships.explanation: Nothing in Roto is illegal, only taboo. A strong taboo culture keeps slave, drug and dark-magic markets confined to the night.
Xi feared the biggest players would write rules that gut Roto from the bottom up. A booming Goldcoral is exactly that player.
relationships.precedent: Roto Kaiishi: Xi on market domination

relationships.short: the heirs check the robber barons
relationships.explanation: Xi built the succession system as "an important counterweight to the often corrupting effects of market domination."
After Xi's death the elite asked for dedicated security. A strong council polices the lower stilts.
The Veil plays no politics until the flesh-born take too much. Then "you can't predict what don't want anything" becomes a warning.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Fenwick; Guinnie's manifest-destiny vote

relationships.explanation: Those who take too much from the earth are "haunted by this tribe and cursed by famine and disease." A roused Veil makes plunder expensive.
relationships.precedent: Fenwick & the Veilwalkers; pirates returning cursed

relationships.short: the earth takes the flesh-born back
relationships.explanation: A mobilized Veil does not burn anyone; "they'd just let the earth take us back."
Those who keep their promises to the Veil "have abundance from whatever item they traded for." The custom itself is agricultural insurance.
The vow-trade only works while the Veil's faith gives vows their weight.
Baba Paku's preaching becomes a culture wherever it takes root.
Unknownism is the district's export and its pride; its spread strengthens Owe Block's sense of itself apart from the spire.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku's quest for the first Owe Block Saint

relationships.short: order leaves no room for heresy
relationships.explanation: Patmos social order and a street-preached heterodoxy compete for the same faithful.

relationships.short: the Cumstead is the family fortune
relationships.explanation: The Line of Johns' wealth is the farm. When it fails, so does the family's purse.
Rump coasts on his family's wealth and reputation to keep the treasurer's office.
relationships.precedent: John Rump: "coasting off the positive reputation of his family"

relationships.explanation: The moral certainty that alcohol is corruption turns, a season later, into people willing to raid a brewery.
The prohibitionist current preaches against the festival first; it is the most visible sin in the Isles.
relationships.precedent: MAA raid on the first Trials

relationships.explanation: Shanty Town has its own purifiers: the Ashen Oath believe grog has tainted the world. A rising prohibitionist current emboldens them and splits the pirate ethos.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town's Political Factions: the Ashen Oath

relationships.short: every Ducket underground is a Ducket untithed
relationships.explanation: Owe Block's informal economy is precisely the money the tithe cannot reach.

relationships.short: the underground trades with the night market
relationships.explanation: Owe Block's underground markets and Roto's after-dark stalls deal in the same goods.
relationships.precedent: A Walk on Owe Block: underground markets

relationships.explanation: The Stank Tank, the Crimson Cutters and the Seaside Circus are culture first; recruits follow the colours.
Stronger gangs run bigger underground markets.
Every retelling of the six-way tie keeps the Kings famous.
The prohibitionist current tells the Kings' story differently: a massacre in a cave, a mayor left in a cage, an assassination.
The Kings' only formal claim to rule is that they are famous for winning. A tarnished legend is a weaker crown.
relationships.precedent: The Age of the Six Kings

relationships.explanation: Visitors come to drink where the Kings drink.
Aleforge's mayors have always handled the festival's logistics; a steady administration puts on a better show.
relationships.precedent: Thomas Thatcher, "in charge of the festival's logistics"; Drake's Revival Fund

relationships.explanation: The Windsunk Council decides "who eats, who raids." A strong Council runs a fatter Shanty.
Shanty runs on reputation, not law. A proud pirate culture draws crews and their plunder.
Roto was built as the pirates' fence; a strong Shanty sends more plunder to the after-dark stalls.

relationships.short: Shanty defines itself against the spire
relationships.explanation: "They call us sinners. We call ourselves free." A stronger Providence hardens the pirate ethos.
A city that prays every three hours does what the spire says.
relationships.precedent: Providence: prayer bells every three hours

relationships.short: the young run off to sea
relationships.explanation: Aleforge's youth "sometimes sneak off to become pirates." A great Trials is also a recruiting fair.
The Trials hire builders and game-makers and fill every shop in town.
Nobody books a room for a festival that was raided last year.
relationships.precedent: The MAA raid on the Trials

relationships.explanation: Goldcoral's owner is a sitting King. A strong Parliament is a strong seat for Jack.

relationships.short: the big player leans on Roto
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral keeps its real books in Roto; as Jack's leverage grows, so does his interest in who Roto's next heir is.
Every step out of isolation widens the Bellows' trade routes.
The Aleforge Special Drinkers Unit has flagged the Bellows; their rise is one more thing the castle is blamed for missing.
Aleforge's government is, in practice, one King's habits. When Seamus is respected, so is the castle; when he is absent from town hall, the castle feels it.
relationships.precedent: Bonehardy elected mayor; "presence in taverns and absence in town hall meetings"

relationships.short: the chain weighs on the man
relationships.explanation: Every calm season in Aleforge is credited to Seamus, and every crisis will be too.
John Rump blackmailed Seamus into legalizing the tonic. The stronger Rump's grip on the treasury, the less of the mayor's office belongs to the mayor.
relationships.precedent: Concept V: Rump "blackmailed Seamus into legalizing the tonic"

relationships.explanation: Seamus "crafted the best trade deals" of the Stewards era; his business sense is the treasury's.
The King of Kegs wrote the Parliament its anthem. His legend and theirs rise together.
relationships.precedent: Compendium III: "his creation of Ode to the Six"

relationships.explanation: Buke was named a candidate for mayor too. A stronger Buke is a standing alternative to Bonehardy.
relationships.precedent: Concept V: "Named candidate for mayor as well"

relationships.explanation: Goldcoral is "privately owned by Jack Anqoak." His fortune and the company's are the same ledger, and it is kept in Roto.
Every profitable Goldcoral voyage lands in one man's coffers.
A Liquor King's name opens doors that a merchant's cannot.
relationships.precedent: Stewards of Aleforge: Goldcoral founded by a sitting King

relationships.explanation: Jack beat Wepple and seized his whole stock. Wepple bartends at the Grog Galley only to watch his ale sold; every gain for Jack is Wepple's loss.
relationships.precedent: Concept V, Turn 9: "Beat and robbed Wepple"

relationships.explanation: Past a point, one King's fortune becomes the Parliament's scandal. The election speeches already call him "a robber baron."
relationships.precedent: Hall of Records: Mayoral Election Speeches

relationships.explanation: Jack spent untold days in Hoegaarden; his fascination brings scholars, and the Kings, back to the library.
Jack ran with the Crimson Cutters in Owe Block. Old colours are not forgotten.
Jagerbauhm grew up a refugee in Providence and argues its case in the Parliament. His standing warms the brittle truce.
Jagerbauhm grew suspicious of Susan Plinket's enthusiasm and exposed her. MAMA fears him more than any other King.
The King who flew into the Dread Harrow and closed the portal is the Parliament's best story.
relationships.precedent: Concept V: "MVP of the final sequence"

relationships.explanation: Faegi's bootleg ClockHeart Tonic made Jagerbauhm a functional alcoholic at sixteen. The stronger the tonic trade, the dearer his habit.
Guinnie came to Shanty Town with nothing, bounced its roughest taverns and built a crew of outcasts. His standing lends the Council weight in Aleforge.
A strong Guinnie makes Aleforge and Shanty Town look like allies.
Guinnie was "the ONLY king to vote for Veilwalker manifest destiny." His rise sours Fenwick on Aleforge.
relationships.precedent: Hall of Records: Mayoral Election Speeches; Concept V: "Anti-Fenwick in policy"

relationships.explanation: A King who backs expansion into the Brush is a King who shrinks the earth-born's ground.
Guinnie's legend is the Trials' legend: an unknown who walked in naked and walked out a King.
Guinnie mowed down Crimson Cutters in every gang confrontation, and Wagwan gave him the Whopper for it.
Buke killed Maximilian. "Not everyone calls it just," and MAMA exists to ask the question. Where the prohibitionist current runs strong, Buke is the villain.
Past a point, Buke's legend stops being a hero story and becomes MAMA's recruiting poster.
Buke is "pro-ale production above all else"; his money and his vote both go to the brewhouses.
When Brewers Lane does well, the King who fought for it gets the credit.
JP speaks for the Veil in the Parliament. A man born in a field that bloomed from spilled drink understands a blessing on the soil.
On the Coors Golden Isles drinking was a faith, and dying of it was ascension. JP's legend feeds the Brewmasters' own.
JP regards the IPA as a fraud tolerated only on the technicality of being alcohol. The Bellows brew the worst IPAs in existence.
"And Jameson Pilsner… out-drank them all." Every great Trials adds a verse.

JP's standing rises with every season Aleforge and Fenwick keep faith.
Buke's legend is Aleforge's drinking legend.
Jack's name as the Oracle of Aleforge was made in Hoegaarden's stacks.

When the vow trade flows, the custom around it holds.
Shanty's fishermen live on Fenwick lures.

relationships.precedent: Old Aleforge Municipal: "They still try to hold onto power"

relationships.explanation: Every power the old offices reclaim is one the castle loses.
Sheriff Cocaine's office was Aleforge's first law. The ASDU is its newest. They do not share.
Drake built the militia to "protect against riots and raids like the ones at the last drunken trials."
A working militia is the castle's best argument that it governs.
The ASDU has flagged the Bellows' routes; a stronger Unit means fewer Ale Bean crates slip through.
Captain Crawdad organized the militia against Drake's interdimensional hordes.
Sergeant Hark's Guard and the Friars are the Cardinal's will made physical.

relationships.short: the Guard in the lower terraces
relationships.explanation: The Guard is how Providence keeps Owe Block a district and not a city.
relationships.precedent: A Walk on Owe Block: Gobbler's law enforcement

relationships.explanation: Tonic leaves Providence one way: through the Guard, or around it.
relationships.precedent: Hunk the Monk; the Whiskey Runners

relationships.explanation: The tithe flows to the spire and the spire pays for its order.
Owe Block's two gangs fight for the same corners. What one takes, the other loses.

relationships.explanation: The Seaside Circus obliterated the Cutters once and would like to again.
relationships.precedent: A Walk on Owe Block: the gang wars

relationships.explanation: The gangs are Owe Block's power; the Cutters are half of it.
The gangs are Owe Block's power; the Circus is the other half.
The Circus sets Owe Block's style as much as its borders.
Dig Dug's mines are "responsible for most of the Gold in the treasury."
Dig Dug is "one of the biggest employers of Oweblock." When the mines hire, the district eats.
Half of all earnings to the spire comes out of miners' wages too.
"The ClockHeart Tonic became both the economy and the religion of the new city."
The Circs brew with chants to the unknown gods; their devotion is the spire's.
A strong spire keeps its tonic clergy in their towers and their vats.
Rump blackmailed the mayor into legalizing the tonic; the runners supply it and he takes his cut.
Every smuggled bottle is one the spire did not sell.

Gobbler was exposed for secretly worshipping the Veilwalkers. A strong Patmos keeps the shrine behind the stone button empty.
Owe Block's underground culture is where Veil sympathy hides.
Every sympathizer in Owe Block is a vow kept far from the Fen.
"Fenwick's nomads tend the island's soul, while we tend its spirit."
The Trials drink from the Deity's spring. Faith in the blessing is faith in the festival.
relationships.precedent: Compendium II (Aleforge: Founding); VI (The Drunken Trials)

relationships.explanation: Aleforge's export is, by its own account, a god's gift. Belief keeps the brewers working and the buyers paying.
To MAMA, alcohol is moral corruption. To the Brewmasters' faithful it is a sacrament. Each side grows at the other's expense.
Each pint on Brewmasters Eve is believed to save one soul. A confident faith drowns out the prohibitionists.
The Liquor Kings are crowned with the Deity's ale.
Past a point, Aleforge's faith turns on its government: Cedric the Vicar claimed to be the Deity reborn and was beheaded; Bronco Chestnut's theocratic turn was voted out.
relationships.precedent: Compendium II (Cedric the Vicar; The Long Thirst)

relationships.explanation: Providence regards Aleforge "with a mix of reverence and righteous scorn"; the two faiths have been rivals since the Monk's exile.
The Ashen Oath and MAMA preach the same sermon from different cliffs.
The Oath is "most dangerous when ignored": zeal becomes organization.
Every season the Oath gains, the grog-soaked freedom Shanty lives on loses ground.
The Tide Callers' faith is Shanty's own: the ocean as a god that punishes arrogance.
Captains who listen to the Tide Callers sail less in bad weather, and fewer policies pay out.

relationships.short: the sea is holy, not tainted
relationships.explanation: The Tide Callers worship the sea the Ashen Oath would purge.
Every wreck season adds to the Coral-eyed; insurers paying out is the sign of it.
The Coral-eyed are part of what makes Shanty Town stranger than anywhere else.
Captains and crews are "the lifeblood of Shanty Town."
Every emboldened crew is a claim waiting to be filed.
relationships.precedent: Banks and Insurance: every pirate raid is a payout

relationships.explanation: Roto was founded to fence pirate plunder. A rich Roto pays well for it.
StormVeil's ships are "the first foreign-flagged vessels the SBN has allowed near its coastline in living memory."
StormVeil made its name on the SBN routes.
Every Albatross depends on wind stores "almost universally sourced by the wind farmers at Wolendi."
Faster ships mean faster money.
The Tankard's brewmaster is "developing a new brew in secret." If he gets free of the Galley, Aleforge gets its best brewer back.
Goldcoral holds Wepple's stock and Wepple's debt.
Nothing sells a Chronicle like a Trials.
The Kings are the Chronicle's favourite subject after Mr. BBL's posterior.
The Owe Block Chronicle "stopped printing the Cardinal's prayer times." A strong spire decides what gets printed.
The underground has its own paper.
Coin for the militia and the ASDU buys patrols, informants and Crawdad's envoys.
Patrols are paid from the treasury.
More patrols, fewer cells.
Drake hired skilled workers to build the games. Money shows.
A bigger Trials draws more visitors.

relationships.explanation: The Revival Fund is paid from the treasury.
The Trials are the thing MAMA's forebears were founded to oppose.
Stricter edicts route more of the market through the spire.

Friars on the corners push the gangs off them.
Every judged market stall is a grievance in the lower terraces.
The tonic sustains the Apostles' ceaseless devotion.
More rations, more brewing.

Tonic handed out is tonic not sold.

Crews that feel robbed stop listening.
The Council rules by deciding who gets tossed.
